newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty board considers restructuring,bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty board considers restructuring,bond deal.

text.p: The Orange County, California Board of Supervisors was expected to consider on Tuesday a proposal to reorganize county government as well as a plan to refund nearly $200 million of taxable pension bonds.
Implementation of the restructuring initiatives could result in the reduction of about 241 full-time positions and county savings of about $11 million a year, officials said.

Orange County Chief Executive Officer Janice Mittermeier first announced the reorganization plan in June. It proposed the elimination of the county's General Services Agency and the transfer of its functions to other departments.

It also called for the elimination of the Environmental Management Agency and the transfer of its functions to other departments or to two new departments -- planning and development services and public works. The plans also outlined a new structure within the county executive office.
The county Board of Supervisors was also expected on Tuesday to adopt a resolution authorizing the tender offer of taxable refunding pension obligation bonds.

The proposal calls for the county to sell about $200 million of debt to refund outstanding 1994 Series A pension bonds. The county's Public Finance Advisory Committee voted earlier this month to approve the plan.
